pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/design/n8n_transform/cli_runner.rs:1372 Arm B claims a slow-but-producing stream survives the shipped ceiling, using real tokio sleeps (8 x 60 ms gaps against a 200 ms lease and a 600 ms ceiling, no paused clock, no tokio test-util), so timer stretch on a loaded or coarse-timer Windows runner can turn it red with no defect present: a stopwatch, not a schedule assertion.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/design/n8n_transform/cli_runner.rs:1372 The cutoff and survival verdicts come from wall-clock sleeps with only ~120 ms total headroom. tokio::time::pause or start_paused would make them about the schedule. prompt_sanitizer.rs:343 (`elapsed.as_millis() < 250`) is a further wall-clock bound, a perf guard on an uncontrolled host.
